title: Client–Server Trust, Authorisation, and Hostile Input Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies client–server trust, authorisation, and hostile input?
options: Treat the app as a public, potentially modified client and enforce ownership and business authority on the server.
Ship a shared admin secret in native code
Trust fields because Play installed the app
Authorise by hiding a button in Compose
questions.answer: Treat the app as a public, potentially modified client and enforce ownership and business authority on the server.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Client-side validation is sufficient when the APK is signed by the legitimate developer.
questions.explanation: Hiding a premium or transfer-authorisation boolean behind R8 still leaves a patchable client decision controlling a server-owned entitlement.

questions.prompt: What must a server check separately from authentication?
questions.answer: Authorisation for the exact resource and action, plus business invariants, replay/idempotency, and abuse limits.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
